analyst_view.overall: Early view: a meeting of two unbeaten sides near the top. Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton have 7 points (4-0 Kauno Zalgiris, 0-0 at Jablonec, 1-0 at Getafe) and Monaco have won all three (2-1 at CSKA Sofia, 3-0 Freiburg, 2-0 Nordsjaelland). The site makes Brighton strong favourites, but Monaco's form says this should be closer than that.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean lower: Brighton have kept clean sheets in 10 of their 13 European games and found it hard to break down Jablonec and Getafe, while Monaco have conceded once in three games and won at home against Nordsjaelland with few chances in a cagey first half.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, most for Brighton. With Brighton at home and likely to have more of the ball, that split looks fair and I have nothing to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. The referee is not known yet and neither side has shown a discipline problem in the competition, so I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, with Brighton on 19. Brighton had plenty of efforts at Getafe (Jaouen Hadjam hit the woodwork twice) but Monaco are a stronger side than the 8.4 shots they are given suggests, so the total looks about right even if the split is more even.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: in their last European games Brighton needed one goal and a lot of misses at Getafe, and Monaco needed only one shot on target to go ahead against Nordsjaelland.
